title: SongForge Connection Saturation
description: Issue #18 follow-up: where the create path runs out of connections, layer by layer. Reading it: under a create-rate ramp you should see the APP's own pool (1) pin at its limit, a big pile of requests waiting on it (2), and creates start failing (3) -- WHILE PgBouncer (4) and the database (5,6) still have headroom. That combination means the app's own connection pool is the wall, not PgBouncer and not the database. Per-process app metrics are sum()'d across web replicas; the DB-derived gauges are already global. Panels 7-9 add the COMPUTE view (web event-loop CPU, and per-container CPU/memory via cAdvisor) -- because the wall is sometimes CPU, not connections, and the pool panels can't show that.

panels.title: 1. App's own DB connections — in use vs limit
panels.description: songforge_db_pool_connections: the app keeps a small, fixed set of connections to talk to the database (through PgBouncer). 'in use' meeting 'limit' means the app's own pool is FULL -- the first wall. Summed across web replicas (each process has its own pool).

panels.title: 2. Requests piling up waiting on the app pool
panels.description: songforge_http_requests_in_flight (requests currently being handled, summed across replicas) vs the app pool limit. The GAP between the two lines is the pile of requests blocked waiting for a free app connection -- your 'N requests in queue'. When in-flight shoots up while the limit line stays flat, the pool is blocking the app.

panels.title: 3. Failed creates per second (pool timeouts, DB rejections & 5xx/503)
panels.description: Which layer is dropping work. pool-timeout = requests that gave up waiting for an APP connection; DB-rejection = Postgres refused a new backend ('too many clients', SQLSTATE 53300) -- the next wall once the app pool is widened; all 5xx/503 = every failed request (overload now returns a graceful 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After, which this still counts). Compare the two specific lines to see whether the app pool or the database is the bottleneck.

panels.title: 4. PgBouncer — DB conversations busy & clients waiting
panels.description: The middle layer. server active = live conversations with the database (of DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE = 20); client waiting = requests queued inside PgBouncer. NOTE: because the app only ever opens ~30 connections to PgBouncer, its waiting line stays SMALL even when the app itself is overwhelmed -- the big backlog lives in panel 2, not here. (Metric names from prometheuscommunity/pgbouncer-exporter; if empty, confirm the exporter's exposed names.)

panels.title: 5. Database — connections in use vs max (100)
panels.description: sum(pg_stat_database_numbackends{datname="songforge"}) vs pg_settings_max_connections. PgBouncer fans everything down to ~20 here, so this should sit FAR below the 100 ceiling -- proving the database itself was never the bottleneck.

panels.title: 6. Database work rate (transactions/sec) — should stay normal
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_database_xact_commit) and rate(pg_stat_database_xact_rollback) for the songforge DB. If these sit at a healthy, steady level while requests are failing upstream, the database is keeping up fine -- the problem is the pool in front of it, not the database's own throughput.

panels.title: 7. Web event-loop CPU per instance (~1.0 = ONE core MAXED = the wall)
panels.description: rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job="songforge_web"}) per web process. Each web container runs ONE uvicorn async event loop = effectively one CPU core, so a line at ~1.0 means that instance is compute-bound and cannot process faster -- the limit the connection/pool panels can't show. If these pin at ~1.0 while the pool (panel 1) and DB (panel 5) sit idle, the bottleneck is CPU, and the fix is more web instances (scale out), not bigger pools.

panels.title: 8. CPU by container (cAdvisor) — who is compute-bound?
panels.description: sum by (name) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{name=~"songforge-.*"})) -- CPU cores used by EVERY container (web, workers, postgres, pgbouncer, simulator, redis, ...). Answers 'what is actually pegged?' at a glance. Requires the cadvisor service (monitoring profile).

panels.title: 9. Memory by container (cAdvisor)
panels.description: container_memory_usage_bytes{name=~"songforge-.*"} -- resident memory per container, to catch a component approaching an OOM. Requires the cadvisor service (monitoring profile).
